quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.textToSpeak: Don't heat it for too long.
quests.hint: Natural sentence, so relax and focus on the stressed word's vowel. Long or short?
quests.explanation: That was "heat": the vowel was long and tense. "Hit" is short and relaxed.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both vowels are front and high, but /ɪ/ sits slightly lower and more relaxed. The sound your ear catches first is the difference in length: /iː/ lasts noticeably longer.
quests.mouthPosition: Try saying /iː/ with a wide, tense smile, then relax the cheeks and shorten the sound; that slack, quick version is /ɪ/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.textToSpeak: I'll pick it up on Friday.
quests.hint: Tight jaw or wide open in the vowel?
quests.explanation: In the sentence, "pick" kept the jaw nearly closed. "Pack" opens the jaw wide.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɪ/ is short and made with the jaw nearly closed; /æ/ is made with the jaw wide open. They are far apart in tongue height, so the biggest cue is how open the mouth is.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɪ/ the jaw barely moves. For /æ/ drop it well down and let the mouth widen.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does the vowel stay short and tight, or open wide and glide?
quests.explanation: You heard "fit": a short, tight vowel that stops quickly. "Fight" opens the jaw wide and glides upward.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɪ/ is a short, tight vowel; /aɪ/ is a longer diphthong that opens wide and then glides up. The jaw movement is much bigger for /aɪ/.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɪ/ keep the jaw nearly closed and stop. For /aɪ/ drop the jaw wide first, then close it as the vowel glides up.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the strong first syllable. Gliding or steady and rounded?
quests.explanation: This time, "waiter" glided upward in the first syllable. "Water" holds a steady rounded vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /eɪ/ is a gliding vowel that ends spread and high; /ɔː/ is a steady, long, rounded vowel with no glide.
quests.mouthPosition: For /eɪ/ start half open and close toward a spread /ɪ/. For /ɔː/ round the lips from the start and hold the shape.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Ask yourself if the first sound would survive with a pinched nose.
quests.explanation: You heard "mall": a nasal hum with the lips closed. "Ball" opens with a lip pop.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The soft palate is lowered for nasals and raised for stops.
quests.mouthPosition: Hum the sound before the vowel.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Wide or half-open vowel before the /nt/?
quests.explanation: In this phrase "rant" used a wide vowel. "Rent" stays half open.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are front vowels, but /æ/ is lower. That extra openness makes /æ/ sound wider and slightly longer than the crisp, short /e/.
quests.mouthPosition: Place a finger under your chin: the jaw should drop noticeably more for /æ/ than for /e/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Decide whether the tongue tip is touching the roof at the start.
quests.explanation: What you caught was "wrap": the tongue curled back with no contact. "Lap" taps the ridge.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /l/ is made with the tongue tip touching the ridge behind the upper teeth, letting air flow around the sides; British /r/ is made with the tongue tip curled slightly back and not touching anything, often with lips a little rounded.
quests.mouthPosition: For /l/ press the tongue tip firmly against the ridge behind the upper teeth. For /r/ curl the tongue tip back and keep it away from the roof of the mouth, lips slightly rounded.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.textToSpeak: I have a good feeling about it.
quests.hint: First syllable, long or short?
quests.explanation: Here, "feeling" had a long, tense vowel. "Filling" clipped it short.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /iː/ is long and tense with the tongue high and forward; /ɪ/ is short, loose and a little lower and more central. Length and tension travel together, so a stretched vowel usually means /iː/.
quests.mouthPosition: For /iː/ spread the lips as if smiling and lift the tongue high behind the lower teeth. For /ɪ/ let the lips relax and drop the tongue a touch.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Smooth hush or stop-plus-hush at the start?
quests.explanation: That was "chips": a stop released into a hush. "Ships" starts with a smooth hush.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʃ/ is a continuous fricative; /tʃ/ begins with a stop and then releases into friction, so it sounds abrupt at the start. Listen for a sudden beginning versus a smooth flow.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ʃ/ let the air flow steadily over the tongue. For /tʃ/ block the air with the tongue against the ridge, then release into a hush.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same start. Is there a hiss before the final /t/?
quests.explanation: In the sentence, "thirty" had no /s/, so the /t/ came right after the vowel. "Thirsty" has a hiss before it.
quests.vowelTensionRule: After /s/, /p t k/ lose their puff of air, so the cluster sounds different from the plain word.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the tongue tip near the ridge for both /s/ and the following /t/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same vowel and nasal. Does anything follow the nasal?
quests.explanation: You heard "rink": a /k/ followed the nasal. "Ring" ends on the nasal alone.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The cluster differs at the end only: /nd/ vs /nt/, /ld/ vs /lt/. Listen for how long the nasal or lateral lasts.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch your throat: buzz continues for the voiced cluster.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same long vowel. Does a stop follow the hiss?
quests.explanation: This time, "past" closed with a /t/ after the /s/. "Pass" ends on the hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The consonant before the last sound is longer when the last one is voiced.
quests.mouthPosition: Shorten the nasal or /l/ before a voiceless stop.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: One vowel glides to schwa. Which?
quests.explanation: It was "beard": the vowel began high and slid to schwa. "Bird" is steady and central.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɪə/ glides from a high front vowel to schwa; /ɜː/ is a steady, long central vowel with no glide. One moves, the other stays put.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɪə/ start with the tongue high and forward, then relax to the centre. For /ɜː/ hold the mouth half open and neutral for the whole vowel.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both long. Rounded or loose lips?
quests.explanation: In this phrase "learn" kept the lips loose. "Lawn" rounds them.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɜː/ sounds neutral and central; /ɔː/ sounds dark and rounded.
quests.mouthPosition: Watch your lips in a mirror: they should stay still for /ɜː/ and round for /ɔː/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Attend to the opening sound: contact at the ridge or a curl away from it?
quests.explanation: You heard "rake": the tongue curled without contact. "Lake" taps the ridge.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Contact versus no contact: /l/ touches the ridge; /r/ hovers below it.
quests.mouthPosition: If your tongue touches the roof, you are making /l/; if it doesn't, /r/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen for the release of the first sound: soft and voiced, or with a puff of breath?
quests.explanation: Here, "beer" began softly. "Pier" starts with a breathy pop.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the start of a word, /p/ is released with a small puff of air (aspiration) and no vocal-fold vibration; /b/ has little or no puff and voicing starts almost immediately.
quests.mouthPosition: Close both lips. For /p/ release them with a clear burst of air; for /b/ release them gently and start the vowel immediately.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Lip burst or buzzing friction?
quests.explanation: That was "berry": the lips popped open. "Very" buzzes with the lip on the teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen for a burst (/b/) versus a buzz (/v/).
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the air flowing without a stop for /v/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Notice how wide your mouth would need to open at the very start of the vowel.
quests.explanation: In the sentence, "now" began wide open. "Know" begins relaxed.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /əʊ/ starts central and ends rounded at /ʊ/ with the mouth closing; /aʊ/ starts with the mouth wide open and closes to /ʊ/. Listen to the start: neutral for /əʊ/, open for /aʊ/.
quests.mouthPosition: For /aʊ/ open the jaw wide first, then round the lips. For /əʊ/ begin with a relaxed, half-open mouth and round gently.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Pay attention to the first half of the vowel: is the mouth half open, or high and narrow?
quests.explanation: The word was "dare": half open. "Dear" starts high and tight.
quests.vowelTensionRule: In careful British English, /ɪə/ begins with a high front vowel and glides to a schwa, while /eə/ begins lower and more open. The start of the vowel tells them apart. (Some speakers flatten /eə/ into a single long vowel, but it stays lower than /ɪə/.)
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɪə/ begin with the tongue high and the jaw nearly shut. For /eə/ begin with the jaw a little more open, then relax into schwa in both.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Wide start or relaxed start?
quests.explanation: This time, "couch" opened wide first. "Coach" begins relaxed.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both end with an 'oo' sound, but /aʊ/ begins much wider.
quests.mouthPosition: Notice the jaw drop at the start of /aʊ/; it does not happen in /əʊ/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Is there a brief stop just before the hush begins?
quests.explanation: It was "sheet": a smooth hush. "Cheat" begins with a stop.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /tʃ/ = /t/ + /ʃ/ in one movement; /ʃ/ has no stop.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the tongue seal against the ridge before release for /tʃ/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does anything pop or burst before the tongue curls back, or does the /r/ come first?
quests.explanation: In this phrase "price" started with a breathy lip pop. "Rice" starts with the curled /r/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: One word has an extra /r/ right after the first consonant. That /r/ makes the beginning of the word sound curled and slightly longer, and the first stop loses some of its crispness.
quests.mouthPosition: After the first consonant, curl the tongue tip back for /r/ before the vowel. Without it, the consonant moves straight into the vowel.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Sharp hiss or soft friction?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "thank": soft, airy friction at the teeth. "Sank" is sharper.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /θ/ is made by placing the tongue tip against or between the teeth and blowing air softly; /s/ is made with the tongue behind the teeth and a narrow groove, giving a sharper hiss.
quests.mouthPosition: For /θ/ let the tongue tip touch the edge of the upper teeth and blow gently. For /s/ pull the tongue back behind the teeth and narrow the air channel.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Which opening is a burst from the lips, and which one is a steady buzz from lip and teeth?
quests.explanation: Here, "bail" opened with a lip pop. "Veil" starts with a buzz between lip and teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /b/ is a stop made by closing the lips fully, with a burst; /v/ is a fricative made with lip and teeth, with continuous buzzing airflow.
quests.mouthPosition: For /b/ press both lips together and release. For /v/ touch the lower lip to the upper teeth and let voiced air flow through.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen for breath in the release of the first sound.
quests.explanation: You heard "crab": a breathy release. "Grab" starts softly.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /k/ is released with a burst of breath before the vowel; /ɡ/ moves directly into the vowel.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the release gentle for /ɡ/ and let the voice start at once.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does a lip pop come before the /l/?
quests.explanation: In the sentence, "lend" began with the tongue-tip /l/. "Blend" starts with /b/ first.
quests.vowelTensionRule: One word begins with an extra consonant that forms a cluster with the next sound. That extra consonant lengthens the start of the word and changes how the following sound is released.
quests.mouthPosition: Say the extra consonant and move directly into the next sound without a vowel between them. Without it, begin straight with the second consonant.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Is there an extra breathy stop at the start?
quests.explanation: The word was "lean": no extra consonant. "Clean" begins with a breathy /k/ before the /l/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: One word begins with an extra consonant that forms a cluster with the next sound. That extra consonant lengthens the start of the word and changes how the following sound is released.
quests.mouthPosition: Say the extra consonant and move directly into the next sound without a vowel between them. Without it, begin straight with the second consonant.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Is there a stop before the /r/?
quests.explanation: This time, "train" put a /t/ before the curled /r/. "Rain" starts with the /r/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: One word begins with an extra consonant that forms a cluster with the next sound. That extra consonant lengthens the start of the word and changes how the following sound is released.
quests.mouthPosition: Say the extra consonant and move directly into the next sound without a vowel between them. Without it, begin straight with the second consonant.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Which final closure is at the lips?
quests.explanation: It was "jog": the back of the tongue closed at the end. "Job" closes at the lips.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen to the vowel transition: it rises into the velar and falls into the bilabial.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the release short and clean.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: A hiss may sit in front of the first stop. Do you catch it?
quests.explanation: In this phrase "stop" began with /s/ and a soft /t/. "Top" begins with a breathy /t/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Adding or dropping /s/ at the start of a cluster changes the word: /sp/, /st/, /sk/ begin with a hiss that is followed by an unaspirated stop. Without /s/, the stop is aspirated and comes first.
quests.mouthPosition: Start with a clear hiss with the tongue behind the teeth, then move directly into the stop. Without /s/, begin with the stop and release with a puff.
